title: Knowledge check: Reviewing an Application for Security

questions.prompt: In Reviewing an Application for Security, which statement best describes Authentication and authorization?
options: Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Authentication verifies an identity. Store password hashes with an established password-hashing library, rate-limit sensitive endpoints, and never log or return credentials.
Define required, optional and rejected values explicitly, validate types and constraints, and return a consistent client error before the data reaches business logic.
questions.answer_key: Authentication verifies an identity. Store password hashes with an established password-hashing library, rate-limit sensitive endpoints, and never log or return credentials.
questions.explanation: Authentication verifies an identity. Store password hashes with an established password-hashing library, rate-limit sensitive endpoints, and never log or return credentials.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Reviewing an Application for Security?
options: Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Plan end-to-end features with acceptance criteria, integrate data and identity components behind clear contracts, review security, test the public API, and release with operational checks and documentation.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
questions.answer_key: Plan end-to-end features with acceptance criteria, integrate data and identity components behind clear contracts, review security, test the public API, and release with operational checks and documentation.
questions.explanation: Plan end-to-end features with acceptance criteria, integrate data and identity components behind clear contracts, review security, test the public API, and release with operational checks and documentation.

questions.prompt: A change related to Reviewing an Application for Security appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
